name: geometry-optimized-no-ids
exporter: Figma - Export > SVG, then SVGO 3 (SVGOMG) on its default preset
story: An ordinary named lower third went through the optimizer every "how to use SVG on the web" article recommends, and came back with no ids, no groups and no whitespace.
idioms: not one id attribute anywhere - SVGO's cleanupIds drops every id nothing references, which is every id a layer name was written into
no <g> wrappers at all: collapseGroups removed them, so there is no ancestor to read a name from either
no XML declaration and no comments (removeXMLProcInst, removeComments)
the whole document on ONE physical line, no indentation, no whitespace between elements
the stylesheet inlined onto the elements and re-minified: style="white-space:pre" with no space after the colon
leading zeros dropped from decimals (fill-opacity=".92", letter-spacing=".08em") and #ffffff shortened to #fff
font-weight="700" as a number rather than Figma's "bold" keyword
attributes reordered into SVGO's own order (width/height before x/y on every rect), and xmlns hoisted to the front of the root
the surviving Figma habits underneath: fractional baselines, one positioned tspan per line, xml:space="preserve", fill="none" on the root
whyThisMatters: Running an SVG through an optimizer is normal, recommended web practice, and the corpus had no file where the layer names are simply GONE - every other fixture tests which of several competing names wins. Here there is nothing to win with, and the promise still standing is that the text layers are found and offered: a name is a convenience, not the mechanism. It is also the only file with no groups and no whitespace between elements, so anything that walks to a parent for a name, or leans on text nodes between tags, meets its worst case. An import that offered zero fields here would tell a student their artwork has no text in it, which is the least true thing it could say.
